entries.title: Tirisfal Glades
body: An eerie land of wooded hills on the northern coast of Lordaeron, under a sky eternally gloomy and tinted a blighted green, where the trees cling to their last shreds of life. Under King Terenas it was a land of peaceful farms and small towns. It was one of the first to fall when the plague of undeath swept through, and mass graves were dug to hold its dead.

Now it is the land of the Forsaken, who rule from the Undercity beneath the ruined capital. Their enemies are never far: the Scourge still haunts the derelict farms and mills, and the Scarlet Crusade holds the Monastery, the seat of its faith, in the north-east. For all its taint, Tirisfal keeps a haunting beauty of its own.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (introduction, Third War and aftermath)

entries.title: Deathknell
body: A small Forsaken village in a well-guarded valley just north of Silverpine, and the only Forsaken settlement that did not keep its old human name; why it was renamed, no one says. Newly risen Forsaken find their feet here.
Deathknell struggles for everything. Its church is held against the "Mindless Ones", the Scourge zombies who overran the north of the village, and the gold mine it needs is infested with spiders.

entries.title: Shadow Grave
body: A crypt at the top of the slope above Deathknell, among the graves along the mountains. It is here that the newly raised Forsaken wake, and Undertaker Mordo greets them.

entries.title: Night Web's Hollow
body: A small valley and gold mine just north-west of Deathknell, infested with spiders. They skitter in the shadows outside and lurk in the webbed galleries within, and in the deepest part of the mine waits the Night Web Matriarch.

entries.title: Solliden Farmstead
body: A pumpkin farm in western Tirisfal, one of the very few places in northern Lordaeron where the living farmers survived the plague. Settlers of Arathor worked land like this as long ago as 2,700 years before the Dark Portal, and noble families from Strom bought it up when they founded Lordaeron.
The Scarlet Crusade protects the Sollidens from the Forsaken and the Scourge, and they are hostile to everyone else. The Forsaken fear the farmers might one day be recruited against them.

entries.title: Brill
body: A small town in the centre of Tirisfal, directly north of the ruined capital, now held by the Forsaken. It was once a town of the kingdom of Lordaeron under the Barov family, and the wealthy Agamands kept a manor here.

Brill was one of the first towns struck by the plague. It was here that Kel'Thuzad, still a living man, began his experiments, and the infection spread so well that the Lich King launched his invasion earlier than planned. The great graveyard outside town was dug for the dead. Magistrate Sevren governs from its town hall, one of only two run by the Forsaken.

entries.title: The Gallows' End Tavern
body: Brill's inn, for a long time the only working tavern run by the Forsaken anywhere. Prisoners are kept in its cellars: a captured Scarlet zealot and a dwarven mountaineer.

entries.title: Agamand Mills
body: A vast network of windmills in the highlands of northern Tirisfal, owned by the Agamands, the most prosperous family in the glades. Now it is probably the largest Scourge outpost in Tirisfal.

When the Scourge came, Gregor Agamand chose to stay and fight, fortified the mills and persuaded his workers to stand with him. They were well stocked and well defended. Then the youngest son, Devlin, betrayed them: he murdered two watchmen and let the undead in where the men slept. A third of the defenders died that night, and the mills could not be held.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Agamand Mills (History, Scourging of Lordaeron)
warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (Second War and aftermath)

entries.title: Agamand Family Crypt
body: The Agamands' crypt just north of the mills, a dark and dusty place. Captain Dargol of the Scourge has settled there and woken every corpse and spirit of the family's dead ancestors, and they attack anyone who enters.

entries.title: Garren's Haunt
body: A large farmstead in northern Tirisfal, once a bountiful place. The Scourge brutally murdered Garren and his family, and the plague turned the land grey and lifeless.
The Rot Hide gnolls have moved into the farm under their leader, Maggot Eye, and dig in the mass graves of the glades for food.

entries.title: Brightwater Lake and Gunther's Retreat
body: The largest lake in Tirisfal, just north-east of Brill. Long ago, fishermen reported a demon stalking its shore; the first Guardian of Tirisfal is said to have fought it on one of the lake's islands.
On the great island in its centre lives Gunther Arcanus, a lich who is free-willed, but believes every other undead is a slave of the Scourge, and sets his zombies on anyone who comes near.

entries.title: Balnir Farmstead
body: A ruined farm north-east of the capital, home of the Balnir family, who bred the great white horses of Lordaeron bought by the royal household. The young Prince Arthas often sneaked out here to play with Jorum Balnir's son, and helped deliver a colt named Invincible, who became his own horse.
When Lordaeron fell, Arthas came back to the ravaged farm and raised Invincible as a skeletal steed. The horse's grave beside the farmhouse has been empty ever since.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (Third War and aftermath)

entries.title: The Bulwark
body: The Forsaken's last line of defence against the Scourge to the east, on the border with the Western Plaguelands, where the sky turns the yellow-grey of the plague lands. The Argent Dawn and the Forsaken hold it together.
During the Scourging of Lordaeron, this was Uther's camp for the survivors of the fallen capital.

entries.title: The Ruins of Lordaeron
body: The remains of the great capital of the kingdom of Lordaeron, destroyed by the Scourge after Arthas betrayed his people. Its palace still stands, and the place is haunted by the last tragic events that led to King Terenas' death and the city's fall.
The palace now serves as the entrance to the Undercity below. Goblin zeppelins tie up outside the walls, carrying travellers to Orgrimmar, Stranglethorn and Northrend.

entries.title: Faol's Rest
body: The grave of Alonsus Faol, the revered archbishop of the Church of the Holy Light, who founded the Order of the Silver Hand and rebuilt Northshire Abbey. He died before the coming of the Scourge, and mourners came here often.
The Scourge raised him from his grave during the Scourging of Lordaeron. The grave now lies untended and mostly forgotten in the shadow of the Scarlet Monastery.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (Third War and aftermath)

entries.title: The Scarlet Towers
body: Scout towers held by the Scarlet Crusade across eastern Tirisfal to guard the approaches to their Monastery. The Scarlet Watch Post covers the Monastery's weaker northern side; the Crusader Outpost watches the main road through the glades.

Near the Monastery's gates lie the Whispering Gardens, where the men who would become the Crusade fought a great battle against the Scourge, and the green Terrace of Repose, one of the very few places in northern Lordaeron the plague never reached.

entries.title: Venomweb Vale
body: A wide valley in eastern Tirisfal, south of the Scarlet Monastery, that was once a green hunting ground for deer and rabbits. Now it is full of deadly spiders.

It was the traditional meeting place of the Council of Tirisfal, the secret order that chose the Guardians, and the first Guardian was empowered here. The spiders were made by a member of the Council, in a mad attempt to protect the meeting place. A rock of fool's gold still marks where Aegwynn met the councillors.

entries.title: Cold Hearth Manor and Stillwater Pond
body: Cold Hearth Manor in central Tirisfal was once known for its warm hearth and bountiful crops. The plague killed everyone who lived or worked there; the Forsaken hold the house now, while mindless zombies wander its barren fields.

Stillwater Pond, west of Brill, was a favourite picnic spot where children swam before they were old enough for the deeper Brightwater. Now it lies grey and forgotten; only the living skeletons of its fish remain.

entries.title: Executor Zygand
body: The commander of Brill's Deathguard, charged with securing the Forsaken's hold on Tirisfal in the name of Queen Sylvanas. His war is with the Scarlet Crusade, whose towers stand within sight of the town.

entries.title: Magistrate Sevren
body: The governor of Brill, who leads the town from his podium in the town hall and hands out the Forsaken's tasks to willing subjects.

entries.title: Coleman and Yvette Farthing
body: Forsaken of Brill who in life were workers and neighbours of the Agamands. They remember the night the mills fell, and Coleman's cold rage against the family who led them to their deaths has not cooled in undeath.

entries.title: Apothecary Johaan
body: A member of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Brill, testing the plants of the glades for the Society's great work: the New Plague.

entries.title: Gunther Arcanus
body: A Forsaken lich who lives on the island in Brightwater Lake with his zombie servants. He is free-willed, but believes every other undead to be a slave of the Scourge, and trusts none of them. The Banshee Queen would like him, and his skill in necromancy, on her side.

entries.title: Before Lordaeron
body: When the Highborne were exiled from Kalimdor, they first landed in Tirisfal and settled among its primitive human tribes. After a few years, many of the elves began to go mad. It was said that something evil slept beneath that part of the world, though it was never proven, and they moved on north to found Quel'Thalas.

The human tribe of Tirisfal was the last to join Thoradin's Arathor, and was won not by force but by respect for its sacred groves and its emblem of a silver hand. Its warrior Lordain became Thoradin's general. Centuries later, nobles of Strom moved north to these fertile lands and founded a city named for him: Lordaeron. For centuries the glades were also the seat of the secret Council of Tirisfal.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (Rise of humanity, The fracturing of Arathor, Guardians of Tirisfal)

entries.title: The Forsaken
body: When the Lich King's power weakened after the Third War, some of the undead he had raised found their minds their own again. Sylvanas Windrunner, once Ranger-General of Quel'Thalas, killed by Arthas and raised as a banshee, led them.

After a civil war in the Plaguelands, Sylvanas and her free-willed undead took the ruined capital and claimed Tirisfal as their home. They call themselves the Forsaken, whatever race they were in life. They joined the Horde as an alliance of convenience, to help them defeat the Lich King.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (Third War and aftermath)

entries.title: The Scarlet Crusade
body: After Lordaeron fell, survivors of the Knights of the Silver Hand under Alexandros Mograine watched the Forsaken move into the ruined capital, and took the deserted Monastery in northern Tirisfal to keep watch. When the Silver Hand splintered, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade grew from it and made the Monastery its sanctuary.
The Crusade is sworn to wipe the undead from Lordaeron, and its fanaticism has turned on anyone it suspects of carrying the plague's taint, living or dead. Its towers stand all across the glades.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tirisfal Glades (Third War and aftermath)
